doc.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011

title: Closing remarks and Beeches memories of making up bridges
summary: Rowe recalls Caramanica improvising bridges to requests; music is great until you must make a living.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Right. You have to be able to show up in a hurry and take advantage of the opportunities and network and everything else. Wow. Well I’ve really enjoyed this conversation.
Why thank you. I had a good time.

You answered a lot of the things that I had wondered about you and I want to thank you because I’ve stolen licks from you over the years. And you know, I remember going way back now to the Beeches where we started, I remember being fascinated because a person would come up and say “Can you guys play ‘Behind Closed Doors’” or some song like that, and you would look at Rick and say what key, and you guys would just play it. And I remember there was times when you guys would get to the bridge and you might not really know it but you would make one up. You’d make up a bridge. I don’t even know if you would remember that.

But you did. And it would make musical sense because you would follow a typical bridge pattern, come back to the A section, and I just thought boy, that is really good. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -23-
Yeah. And I guess it goes back to learning stuff by ear and listening to the radio.
Well when you have to eat on it you learn how to do that stuff.

You know you told me something once and I said to myself wow, I remember saying wow. Because you said music is great until you have to make a living at it. I think I may be paraphrasing you. But it was a very on-target, practical piece of advice.
Yeah. Something we learned the hard way.
